sources.title: Australian population grid 2024
sources.population: Estimated Resident Population (usual residents). The grid distributes SA1 estimates over residential address points, Indigenous Community Points or fallback SA1 centroid points, then sums into 1 km² cells.
sources.measure: Modelled density, people per km²; NOT a growth rate, household count, migrant flow or urban/rural classification
sources.geography: Australia, National Nested Grid; 2021 SA1/ASGS Edition 3 inputs; EPSG:3577. Lesson adaptation shows mainland and Tasmania, excludes distant-island margins.
sources.adaptation: Native JPEG reduced decode, proportional crop, resampling, state/territory region labels, title and verified legend added. No invented geometry or recolouring. Reduced cells blend: only broad patterns are assessed; exact per-cell numerical extraction is not supported.
sources.comparability: Same 2024 reference/release as B, but grid cells and GCCSAs are different spatial units. No one-to-one equivalence between coloured cells and complete city boundaries; no density ranking calculated from B.
sources.limitations: 2024 ERP preliminary in this release; estimates may be revised. Modelled cell allocation and national-scale reduction limit precision. Grey is a model category, not proof of no community, activity, cultural connection or occupation. No causal/migration/job inference is established by the map.
sources.rights: © Commonwealth of Australia. CC BY 4.0 confirmed in supplied grid metadata and official ABS-owned item. No logo/Coat of Arms/third-party basemap reproduced.
sources.publicationRequirements: Retain ABS attribution, original release/source link, licence reference, adaptation notice and limitations. Do not imply ABS endorsement.

sources.title: Population change by capital city — four selected rows
sources.reference: ERP at 30 June 2024; change from 30 June 2023 to 30 June 2024
sources.population: Usual-resident ERP. Foreign diplomatic personnel/families excluded. June 2024 preliminary in this release; June 2023 revised.
sources.measure: Residents (count); added residents over one year (count change); percentage increase relative to the starting population (growth rate, rounded to 1 decimal place). Not urban share or density.
sources.geography: Greater Capital City Statistical Areas (GCCSA), ASGS Edition 3. Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth only; not all capitals, all urban areas, or equal-area regions.
sources.comparability: Within-release count/growth comparisons are valid for these defined city regions. Boundaries include non-urban land; do not treat their sum as national urban population or compare to national/DEGURBA urban percentages.
sources.limitations: A deliberately dated teaching snapshot, not latest population data. Later revisions must not be mixed into this table. Missing national totals, urban classifications and land areas prevent urbanisation or density calculations.
sources.rights: © Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0. Four factual rows transcribed; no ABS branding or third-party graphic copied.
sources.publicationRequirements: Retain source, reference periods, units, geography, selection and preliminary/revision caveat.

sources.title: Regional population methodology, 2023–24
sources.use: ERP definition, estimation/revision status and limits. The grid XML additionally documents the spatial allocation method.
sources.rights: Paraphrased factual methodology, attributed to ABS. No third-party material reproduced.

sources.title: World Urbanization Prospects 2025 — Glossary of Demographic Terms
sources.use: Concepts only: urbanisation as rising urban share, national definitions, density and settlement hierarchy. No UN numerical population series, image, logo or text block reproduced.
sources.comparability: National urban definitions and the Degree of Urbanization are different systems. No numerical claim about Australia’s urban share is derived from the ABS GCCSA table.
sources.rights: Original paraphrased explanation and previously approved original G03 illustrative diagram. No reuse claim over UN artwork.
